{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (for Customer / Sparkling) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement 
**Status:** 19 rules assessed — 6 deviations (3 critical), 2 missing, 11 compliant

## Executive summary

The Agreement is, on balance, unusually customer-favourable on the commercial levers we care most about. There is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum-volume or take-or-pay commitment, no MFN, no auto-renewal trap, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, and no audit right running against us. We hold an unqualified 90-day convenience termination right (Garman holds none), a one-year-plus conformance warranty with real remedies, and a perpetual, fully-paid escrow licence.

Four items need to be fixed. Two are walk-away issues under our playbook: the blanket assignment consent with no affiliate or successor carve-out for us (Page 10 / § 20(d), reinforced by § 3(c)), and the mutual **no-hire** in § 19, which reaches any employee of either party with no general-advertising carve-out. Two further critical points are the ownership position in § 13 — Garman takes the Schedule "D" Modifications and Improvements built for us, with only a narrow non-transferable use licence back and silence on ownership of our data — and § 15, which is mutual and carves out §§ 13 and 14 but contains **no monetary cap at all**, leaving direct-damages exposure unlimited on both sides. We have also inserted the two missing clauses: post-termination transition assistance and data return (§ 17 has no exit path for our data, including data converted under § 4), and a standard vendor insurance covenant, given that Garman's personnel work on site and handle our data. Governing law (Nova Scotia) is off our accepted list but is a low-heat point.

Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule) was not provided; several "compliant" conclusions on pricing-adjacent rules are subject to review of that schedule.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (at fallback) | Page 6 |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation (walk-away)** | Page 10 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant (at fallback) | § 2 Grant of License |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | § 17 Term and Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Page 8 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Page 10 |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 10 Maintenance and Support |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 17 Term and Termination |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 12 Specifications and Warranty |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Page 11 |

### Detail on the items we are redlining

- **IP / ownership (§ 13).** Garman owning its base Software is acceptable, but § 13 also vests the Modifications and Improvements — including the Schedule "D" Modifications built for us — in Garman, while our only licence back (§ 2) is a non-transferable, non-exclusive right to use the "Software" at Authorized Locations with no right to modify or sublicense. The Agreement is silent on ownership of our data, including data converted under § 4. That falls short of the fallback licence-back. We have added a Sparkling data-ownership sentence and a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence covering Improvements and Modifications.
- **Limitation of liability (§ 15).** Mutual, excludes indirect and consequential damages, and carves out §§ 13 and 14 — but with no cap, it fails the fallback requirement of a mutual cap at 12 months' fees. We have added the mutual greater-of cap (12 months' fees / USD 1,000,000), expanded carve-outs to gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmed our fee obligations are not "damages".
- **Assignment (Page 10, § 20(d) with § 3(c)).** Blanket consent, no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for us, no reasonableness standard. We have added the affiliate/successor carve-out, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard for other assignments, and confirmation that a change of control of Sparkling gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right.
- **Non-solicitation (§ 19).** This is a no-hire, not a non-solicit, reaching "any employee of the other party" rather than personnel involved in the services, with no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches. We have narrowed it to a mutual 12-month non-solicitation of directly involved personnel with standard carve-outs; mutuality is preserved.
- **Transition assistance (§ 17 — missing).** Termination obligations run one way: we stop using and return the Software, with no transition assistance, no return or export of our data (including converted data in Garman's possession) and no deletion certification. Escrow under § 16 gives continuity of the Software only, not an exit path. We have inserted a new § 17(d): six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable form within 30 days, and certified deletion. Fallback: 90 days' assistance.
- **Insurance (Page 11 — missing).** No insurance covenant anywhere, yet Garman's personnel install, convert our data and train on site (§§ 4, 5, 9). We have inserted our standard paragraph as § 20(k) (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where our data is processed, certificates on request). Fallback: E&O 1M / cyber 2M.
- **Governing law (Page 10).** Nova Scotia law and courts sit outside our accepted list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales as fallback), so the clause fails both positions. Low heat: venue is non-exclusive and Nova Scotia is our own home province, not Garman's (Saskatchewan). We have proposed New York and will accept any name on the accepted list.

### Noted, not flagged

- **Indemnity (Page 6):** sits at the fallback. We would prefer express defence/settlement-control mechanics, a refund remedy, and "prompt written notice" in place of the 10-day claim-notice requirement, but § 15 expressly places § 13 outside the liability limitation, so the indemnity is neither capped nor gutted and no reciprocal indemnity is imposed on us.
- **Licence scope (§ 2):** covers our affiliated companies without a notice condition and is not revocable at Garman's discretion. Contractors acting on our behalf are not named; transferability to a successor is handled in the assignment redline rather than flagged twice.
- **Convenience termination (§ 17):** at the fallback (90 days rather than 30). No express pro-rata refund of prepaid maintenance on a convenience exit — we would add this if the document is reopened.
- **Renewal (§ 10):** no cap on renewal-year maintenance price increases in the body of the Agreement; we would add a CPI/3% cap if reopened.
- **Warranty (§ 12):** exceeds our preferred 12-month period; no express "professional and workmanlike" / compliance-with-laws warranty for the on-site services.

## Walk-away items

1. **Blanket assignment consent (Page 10, § 20(d), reinforced by § 3(c))** — no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard. Our playbook treats this as walk-away territory; the carve-out and reasonableness standard must land.
2. **Mutual no-hire (§ 19)** — no-hire provisions are walk-away territory under our playbook. Conversion to a narrow 12-month non-solicit of directly involved personnel, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, is required.

We would also treat the wholly uncapped direct-damages exposure in § 15 combined with Garman's ownership of the Modifications built for us (§ 13) as a package that must move before signature, even though neither is labelled walk-away on its own.

## Next steps

1. Send the redline covering the six items above (IP/data ownership, liability cap, assignment, non-solicit, transition assistance, insurance) plus the governing-law swap, flagging the two walk-away items as such to Garman.
2. Obtain **Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule)** and confirm it contains no sole-source, MFN, minimum licence count, committed maintenance year or price-escalation language; our compliant conclusions on EXCLUSIVITY, LD, MFN, MINCOMMIT and RENEWAL are subject to that review.
3. Obtain **Schedule "D" (Modifications)** to scope precisely which deliverables are caught by the § 13 ownership provision, so we can size the licence-back if Garman resists an ownership change.
4. Confirm with the business the acceptable fallbacks: 90 days' transition assistance, E&O 1M / cyber 2M insurance, and any accepted-list governing law other than New York.
5. If the document is reopened for other reasons, add the pro-rata refund of prepaid maintenance on convenience exit, a CPI/3% renewal price cap, and a services-quality warranty."}
